 18→
 19→1. **The campaign discriminates.** T = TOP/CH5 (CFC-180) spans
 20→   **0.893 → 1.062 (16.8 %)** across the 8 specimens with within-specimen CV
 21→   0.17–0.48 % — every adjacent pair in the ranking separates at |d| ≥ 2.8.
 22→   **`6lhxfy` (Sobol spec 01) is the first strong attenuator ever measured
 23→   under this SOP (T = 0.893)**, reproduced across two sessions on different
 24→   days to 0.13 %.
 25→2. **A processing fix was required first** (§2): the carriage now arrives
 26→   fast enough that mat contact starts > 2 ms before the 150 G trigger, so
 27→   the 2 ms pre-trigger window rides a +10–20 G contact foot and is no longer
 28→   a valid baseline. Without the fix, Δv reads catastrophically low and — more
 29→   importantly — **T carries a specimen-dependent bias of up to ~5 %**, which
 30→   would have scrambled the BO objective. The fixed pipeline re-baselines on
 31→   the record tail and was validated against the TP4 series tables'
 32→   independent per-event Δv and raw peaks (agreement 1–3 %).
 33→3. **The tower is healthy.** On the corrected (and TP4-corroborated) scale,
 34→   input Δv was 5.03–5.45 m/s all week — at or near the healthy-tower bar —
 35→   and it *improved* through the week (§3). The standing "tower still at
 36→   ~87 % of free-fall" narrative from the 08-10/08-12 sessions was largely
 37→   the same baseline artifact and is corrected below.
 38→4. **For the BO hand-off** (§5): `campaign_summary.csv` has one row per
 39→   specimen with objectives ± sd and design parameters. Two blockers on the
 40→   metadata side: **`amdjwm` (2nd-best specimen, T = 0.980) appears in no
 41→   print key anywhere** — its design parameters are unknown — and the
 42→   `ebdna8` session seen on the TP4 status bar on 08-18 has not been
 43→   uploaded.
 44→
 45→## 1. Sessions
 46→
 47→| specimen | Sobol spec | session (start) | captures | notes |
 48→|---|---|---|--:|---|
 49→| `bag26v` | 08 | 08-13 13:56 | 101/101 | earliest; 5 days before the rest; pre-settings-reset |
 50→| `amdjwm-s1` | **unknown** | 08-17 11:33 | 87/87 | interrupted first attempt |
 51→| `amdjwm` | **unknown** | 08-17 13:57 | 101/101 | full re-run, same day |
 52→| `bpx68c` | S0 (ref) | 08-17 15:19 | 101/101 | = the calibration-check "before" set |
 53→| `autv5r` | 02 | 08-19 15:34 | 103/103 | 2 extra captures (S103/104) after end-of-session pauses — normal drops, kept |
 54→| `6lhxfy-s1` | 01 | 08-19 17:09 | 35/35 | interrupted first attempt |
 55→| `6lhxfy` | 01 | 08-20 13:15 | 101/101 | full re-run next day |
 56→| `9hhbkp` | 00 | 08-20 14:34 | 101/101 | |
 57→| `nvxsrv` | 04 | 08-20 16:13 | 101/101 | one 13 min pause after drop 44 |
 58→| `6nheas` | 05 | 08-20 18:02 | 101/101 | ends 08-21 01:24 UTC |
 59→
 60→942/942 captures are clean real drops — **zero invalid/spurious triggers in
 61→the entire batch**, no channel above 4.7 % of full scale, median cadence
 62→~41–45 s. The 08-13/08-17 sessions predate the 08-18 TP4 settings reset; the
 63→calibration check already verified continuity across it.
 64→
 65→## 2. The pre-trigger contact foot, and why the pipeline needed a fix
 66→
 67→The abc123-era convention baselines every channel on the median of the 2 ms
 68→pre-trigger window. That was valid when it was written. In this batch the
 69→pre-trigger is **not quiet**: CH5 sits +10 to +20 G above the record tail for
 70→the full 2 ms before the trigger (bag26v, the slowest session: +2 G;
 71→08-19/20 sessions: +16 to +20 G). At 5.4 m/s the carriage crosses the mat's
 72→12.7 mm thickness in ~2.3 ms, so early mat compression is already underway
 73→more than 2 ms before the 150 G crossing — the entire pre-trigger window
 74→rides the contact foot.
 75→
 76→Consequences of baselining on the foot:
 77→
 78→- **Δv collapses.** The 15 ms Δv integral picks up the (−foot) offset over
 79→  its whole window: sessions read 2.0–3.5 m/s instead of ~5.3 m/s, and the
 80→  bias *grows within a session* as the mat warms and the foot lengthens —
 81→  manufacturing an apparent "velocity decay" that is not real.
 82→- **T is biased per-specimen.** Peaks are measured relative to the wrong
 83→  zero, and the foot differs between CH5 and the top-vertex channels (they
 84→  see it through different paths), so T shifted by up to ~5 % in a
 85→  specimen-dependent way (e.g. `nvxsrv` 1.074 → 1.024 after the fix,
 86→  `autv5r` 1.077 → 1.041, while `bpx68c` barely moved 1.011 → 1.011).
 87→
 88→**The fix** (committed): `analyze_capture` gains a `baseline="tail"` mode —
 89→each channel is re-zeroed on its median over the final 30 ms of the 100 ms
 90→record — and the campaign pipeline uses it for all sessions. The
 91→default `"pretrigger"` mode is untouched, so every previously committed
 92→analysis reproduces unchanged. Validation against the TP4's own series
 93→tables (computed independently by the DAQ from raw data): per-event CH5 raw
 94→peaks agree to 1–2 %, per-event Δv to 2–3 %, across all 10 sessions. On
 95→clean-pretrigger sessions the two baselines coincide, so the corrected scale
 96→remains comparable to the healthy-tower references.
 97→
 98→**Correction to the standing record.** The same artifact was already
 99→present, smaller, in the 08-10/08-12 rail-maintenance sessions (their TP4
100→series tables read 0.3–0.4 m/s higher than the committed pipeline values,
101→with the gap growing across the week). Two standing conclusions soften:
102→the "settled at 4.55–4.66 m/s ≈ 87 % of free-fall" plateau was an
103→underestimate (TP4 scale: 4.9–5.0 m/s and still rising), and the within-
104→session "mat-rebound decay" in Δv was partly the foot growing rather than
105→physics. Correction notes have been added to the speed-decay and
106→pre/post-grease docs. The qualitative conclusions (greasing produced a real
107→step; no cumulative decay over 100 drops) survive.
108→
109→## 3. Rig health: the tower quietly finished recovering
110→
111→Input Δv (corrected pipeline, corroborated by TP4) by session:
112→
113→| date | session(s) | Δv (m/s) | % of 5.47 free-fall |
114→|---|---|--:|--:|
115→| 08-10 | pre/post-grease | 4.6 (TP4) | 84 % |
116→| 08-11 / 08-12 | speed-decay | 4.9 / 5.0 (TP4) | 90–91 % |
117→| 08-13 | `bag26v` | 5.03 (rising within session) | 92 % |
118→| 08-17 | `amdjwm-s1` / `amdjwm` / `bpx68c` | 5.01 / 5.26 / 5.30 | 92–97 % |
119→| 08-19 | `autv5r` / `6lhxfy-s1` | 5.34 / 5.51 | 98–101 %* |
120→| 08-20 | `6lhxfy` / `9hhbkp` / `nvxsrv` / `6nheas` | 5.37 / 5.45 / 5.33 / 5.26 | 96–100 %* |
121→
122→\* Δv is the full-pulse integral = arrival + rebound speed, so it can
123→slightly exceed the free-fall *arrival* figure; values at ~100 % imply
124→arrival within a few percent of free fall with a small mat rebound.
125→
126→The greasing recovery did not stall at the 08-12 "settled" level — it kept
127→improving with traffic, and by campaign week the tower was effectively at
128→the healthy-tower bar (abc123 healthy reference 5.28–5.35 m/s). Every
129→campaign session lands in a ±4 % Δv band, so impact severity is matched
130→across specimens to about the same tolerance as the input peak (in180
131→203–232 G, partly specimen-mass-dependent).
132→
133→## 4. Campaign results
134→
135→### 4.1 Ranking (stabilized drops, warm-up 2 discarded)
136→
137→| rank | specimen | spec | T180 (CV) | T1000 | e_rebound | t_second | fn / ζ (usable frac) |
138→|--:|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
139→| 1 | `6lhxfy` | 01 | **0.8931 (0.47 %)** | 0.913 | 0.0504 | 55.2 ms | 368 Hz / 10.2 % (0.64) |
140→| 2 | `amdjwm` | ? | **0.9805 (0.26 %)** | 1.007 | 0.030† | 31.8 ms† | 455 Hz / 9.6 % (0.05) |
141→| 3 | `6nheas` | 05 | **0.9970 (0.32 %)** | 0.996 | 0.0402 | 43.2 ms | 322 Hz / 19.3 % (1.00) |
142→| 4 | `bpx68c` | S0 | 1.0111 (0.23 %) | 1.067 | 0.0204 | 22.1 ms | 468 Hz / 16.7 % (0.01) |
143→| 5 | `9hhbkp` | 00 | 1.0183 (0.17 %) | 1.028 | 0.0215 | 23.9 ms | 364 Hz / 11.2 % (0.58) |
144→| 6 | `nvxsrv` | 04 | 1.0275 (0.43 %) | 1.230 | 0.0266 | 28.9 ms | 294 Hz / 31.0 % (0.88) |
145→| 7 | `autv5r` | 02 | 1.0404 (0.34 %) | 1.136 | 0.0268 | 29.2 ms | 386 Hz / 6.4 % (0.39) |
146→| 8 | `bag26v` | 08 | 1.0616 (0.48 %) | 1.242 | 0.0241 | 24.7 ms | — (0.00) |
147→
148→† `amdjwm`'s secondary-event detector is bimodal (CV ~49 %) — its hop lands
149→near a ringdown lobe and the picker alternates between two candidates; its
150→t_second/e_rebound are not reliable this session. All other specimens have
151→e_rebound CV ≤ 4.3 %.
152→
153→ANOVA on T180: F ≈ 2.4 × 10³, p ≈ 0 across 8 specimens; spread 16.8 % with
154→median within-specimen CV 0.33 %. Adjacent-pair gaps and effect sizes
155→(Welch): 6lhxfy→amdjwm 9.8 % (|d| = 25), amdjwm→6nheas 1.7 % (5.7),
156→6nheas→bpx68c 1.4 % (5.0), bpx68c→9hhbkp 0.7 % (3.5), 9hhbkp→nvxsrv 0.9 %
157→(2.8), nvxsrv→autv5r 1.2 % (3.3), autv5r→bag26v 2.0 % (4.8). Figures:
158→[series](../data/drop-tests/sobol-campaign/figures/01_campaign_series.png) ·
159→[ranking](../data/drop-tests/sobol-campaign/figures/02_campaign_ranking.png).
160→
161→**Honest tiering against the known noise floors** (print-to-print ≈ 2 %
162→spread in T; cross-session mount re-seat ≤ ~2 %): the ranking resolves into
163→four design-level tiers — **`6lhxfy` alone** (9.8 % clear of everything),
164→**`amdjwm`/`6nheas`** (attenuating-to-neutral), **the near-unity middle**
165→(`bpx68c`/`9hhbkp`/`nvxsrv`, spanning 1.6 % — *not* mutually resolved at the
166→print level), and **the amplifiers** (`autv5r`, `bag26v`). Within-tier order
167→is statistically real for *these articles* but should not be read as a
168→design difference.
169→
170→### 4.2 The headline: `6lhxfy` (spec 01)
171→
172→T = 0.893 — an 11 % peak reduction relative to the base input, where every
173→previously measured specimen sat within a few % of 1.0 (best ever before:
174→`yqpmx1` ≈ 0.96 at 13 in on the retired hot-glue mount). Its design corner:
175→**thickest struts (9.24 mm), thinnest cables (2.55 mm), highest twist
176→(77.4°), lightest mass (18.50 g)** — the compliant-cable/stiff-strut corner
177→of the Sobol box. It is also the biggest hopper (e_rebound 0.050, hop
178→landing at ~55 ms) and holds T1000 = 0.913, i.e. it attenuates broadband,
179→not just in the CFC-180 band. The BO prior should treat this corner as the
180→live region.
181→
182→### 4.3 Session-to-session repeatability — the free crossover checks
183→
184→The two interrupted sessions are independent re-runs (fresh mount seating,
185→different day for `6lhxfy`):
186→
187→| specimen | session 1 | session 2 | ΔT180 |
188→|---|--:|--:|--:|
189→| `6lhxfy` | 0.8943 (35 drops, 08-19) | 0.8931 (101 drops, 08-20) | **0.13 %** |
190→| `amdjwm` | 0.9862 (87 drops, 08-17 am) | 0.9805 (101 drops, 08-17 pm) | 0.58 % |
191→
192→Both land well inside the ~2 % re-seat envelope — T180 is transferring
193→across sessions far better than the historical worst cases. **T1000 does
194→not transfer** (`amdjwm` 1.159 → 1.007; `6lhxfy` 1.029 → 0.913): the
195→broadband ratio is dominated by mount-coupling HF content, confirming the
196→long-standing choice of CFC-180 T as the primary objective and T1000 as a
197→secondary/diagnostic only. (`autv5r` also drifts +15 % in T1000 *within*
198→its session while T180 stays flat — same lesson.)
199→
200→### 4.4 Drift, ringdown, secondary metrics
201→
202→- **T180 drift within sessions is negligible**: |slope| ≤ 0.016 %/drop
203→  (most ≤ 0.008 %), the two largest with the usual first-drops mat
204→  transient. 101 drops per specimen buys a ±0.05 % standard error on T —
205→  100× tighter than the print-to-print floor; 5–10 recorded drops would
206→  give the same design information (the standing sample-size result).
207→- **e_rebound** spans 0.020–0.050 (2.5×) and correlates with attenuation
208→  (the two best T specimens hop hardest — consistent with energy leaving
209→  through the compliant-cable path rather than transmitting). It remains
210→  the sharpest per-drop discriminator (CV ≤ 2 % for most specimens).
211→- **Ringdown fits** are usable for 5 of 8 specimens (fn 294–468 Hz,
212→  ζ 6–31 %). `bag26v` (0 % usable, the tallest article at H = 105 mm) and
213→  `bpx68c`/`amdjwm` (≤ 5 %) fail the r² gate — their post-impact envelope
214→  is not a single decaying mode. Treat fn/ζ as opportunistic secondary
215→  outputs, not campaign objectives.
216→- **Mat state**: CH5 raw stayed ≤ 4.7 % of full scale everywhere; the PU
217→  mat needed no attention across 942 drops.
218→
219→## 5. BO hand-off
220→
221→[`figures/campaign_summary.csv`](../data/drop-tests/sobol-campaign/figures/campaign_summary.csv)
222→carries one row per specimen: `t180`, `t1000`, `out_180_g`, `in_180_g`,
223→`in_dv_ms`, `t_second_ms`, `e_rebound`, `fn_hz`, `zeta_pct` (mean ± sd
224→each), Δv health verdict, and the design parameters (R, H, twist, strut Ø,
225→cable Ø, mass, spec index) joined from `params.json`. Recommended objective
226→column: `t180_mean` (with `t180_sd`); `e_rebound_mean` as a secondary
227→objective if the BO goes multi-output.
228→
229→**Open items blocking a complete design table:**
230→
231→1. **`amdjwm` maps to no known print.** It is absent from the `.3mf` print
232→   key, the Sobol design table, and every issue/PR in the repo. Its
233→   parameters are blank in the CSV. @me-madsen — which spec is it (a
234→   re-print of 03/06/07? a re-label?), and can its mass be added?
235→2. **`ebdna8` (spec 03)**: the 08-18 TP4 settings screenshot showed the
236→   database sitting on a completed session `ebdna8 - 60 in - 1/2" mat -
237→   101 drops`, but no `ebdna8` upload exists. If that session is real,
238→   uploading it may complete a 9th specimen for free.
239→3. The 9th specimen (tested "tomorrow morning" per the posting comment) and
240→   the slow-motion videos are pending; the pipeline is one command to
241→   re-run when they land.
242→4. Spec 08's official article: the print key flags `dea4ls` (per the .3mf)
243→   vs `bag26v` (per the issue comment) — `bag26v` is what was tested here.
244→
245→## 6. Caveats
246→
247→- **n = 1 article per design** (except the two double-session specimens,
248→  which replicate *sessions*, not prints). The print-defect study put
249→  print-to-print scatter at ~2 % in T — that is the design-resolution
250→  floor for this table, and why the middle tier is unresolved.
251→- `bag26v` ran 5 days before the rest on a slightly slower tower
252→  (Δv 5.03 vs 5.26–5.45); T is severity-robust, but its last-place margin
253→  (2.0 % below `autv5r`) is larger than any plausible session effect.
254→- The Δv health bands in the script were derived on the pre-trigger
255→  baseline; they remain valid on the corrected scale because the two
256→  estimators coincide on clean-pretrigger (healthy-era) data, but
257→  sub-0.1 m/s comparisons across the estimator change should not be made.
258→- `amdjwm`'s t_second/e_rebound are unreliable this session (§4.1 †).
259→- The 2 ms pre-trigger is now structurally too short for a quiet baseline
260→  at healthy-tower speeds. The tail baseline handles it in analysis, but if
261→  the TP4 allows a longer pre-trigger (e.g. 5 ms = 5 %), the foot would be
262→  fully in-record and the estimator debate disappears at the capture level.
263→
264→## 7. Addendum (2026-08-21): why the printed masses vary despite the constant-mass constraint
265→
266→@sgbaird flagged that the measured masses (18.50–22.04 g, CV 5.9 %) vary
267→more than expected given the batch generator's constant-mass constraint
268→(PR #35, `bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py`).
269→
270→**The constraint was implemented and converged.** Route A projects every
271→Sobol design onto the constant-mass manifold by uniform re-scaling, with
272→m\* = 30.95 g defined as the *solid-volume* mass of the S0 reference STLs
273→(ρ_PLA = 1.24, ρ_TPU = 1.21 g/cm³). The committed
274→`bo/t3-prism-bo-batch.csv` shows all 9 designs at 30.90–30.97 g predicted
275→(`mass_ok=True`, tolerance ±0.15 g).
276→
277→**The gap is solid volume vs printed mass.** The slicer prints the PLA
278→struts/joints/housings with walls + sparse infill but the thin TPU cables
279→essentially solid. Regressing the 7 measured masses on the CSV's predicted
280→per-material solid masses (S0's split, 23.42 g PLA + 7.53 g TPU, computed
281→from the committed reference STLs):
282→
283→```
284→measured ≈ 0.565 · m_PLA,solid + 0.986 · m_TPU,solid   (R² = 0.78, resid sd 0.64 g)
285→```
286→
287→PLA prints at ~57 % of solid, TPU at ~99 %. Because the constant-mass
288→projection preserves shape ratios, the PLA/TPU split varies strongly by
289→design (TPU fraction 12–36 %), so each gram of solid mass the design moves
290→from PLA to TPU adds ~0.42 g of printed mass. That deterministically maps
291→the constant-solid-mass batch onto an ~±9 % printed-mass spread — e.g.
292→`6lhxfy` (spec 01, TPU fraction 0.118) is the lightest at 18.50 g while the
293→TPU-rich `9hhbkp`/`6nheas` (0.35–0.36) sit at 21.6–21.7 g. The ±0.3–0.8 g
294→residuals are true print-to-print variance (~3 %), consistent with the
295→print-defect study.
296→
297→**Fix for future batches** (in `bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py` on PR #35):
298→either weight the scale solve's per-material volumes by effective print
299→densities (0.565 / 0.986 as fitted — one-line change, but profile-dependent),
300→or iterate the solve on the BambuStudio CLI's sliced per-filament grams,
301→which is exact for the active print profile. Which is "right" depends on
302→what the constraint is for: if the BO comparison is per-gram-of-printed-
303→structure, printed mass is the physical quantity to hold constant.
304→
305→**Side effect worth using:** the fit predicts printed masses for the
306→untested specs — 03 (`ebdna8`) ≈ 20.4 g, 06 ≈ 19.2 g, 07 ≈ 21.5 g. Weighing
307→`amdjwm` (§5 open item 1) against these would help disambiguate which spec
308→it is (a ~19 g reading points at 06, ~21.5 g at 07).

1→# Print-defect study — five nominally identical T3-prism prints
  2→
  3→**Specimens** `57vqhx`, `mdt6ja`, `j1crxg`, `cruela`, `bpx68c` ·
  4→**502 captures** (~100 per specimen) · **60 in** · 4 felt + 1 cardboard ·
  5→2026-07-28 / 07-29 · 4-channel 1.25 MHz / 20 ms exports.
  6→
  7→Data posted by @me-madsen on PR #86
  8→([comment 5136111762](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/pull/86#issuecomment-5136111762),
  9→Box folder `oii429e3znjusbltzg56h5kwbi5cj29n`); defect photos/video on
 10→[PR #35 comment 5110159623](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/pull/35#issuecomment-5110159623)
 11→and the one below it.
 12→Raw: [`data/drop-tests/print-defects/`](../data/drop-tests/print-defects/) ·
 13→Script: [`scripts/analysis/drop_test_print_defects_analysis.py`](../scripts/analysis/drop_test_print_defects_analysis.py) ·
 14→Metrics: `data/drop-tests/print-defects/figures/print_defects_metrics.json`.
 15→
 16→All five specimens come from the same T3-prism model/configuration; the question
 17→is **how much printing defects move the drop-test result**. Specimen IDs are
 18→lower-cased throughout per @me-madsen's request to treat them case-insensitively.
 19→
 20→---
 21→
 22→## 1. Headline
 23→
 24→**Print-to-print scatter in transmissibility is ~0.7 % CV (1.95 % spread across
 25→five copies) — small in absolute terms, but the same size as the between-*design*
 26→differences the 60 in campaign has been reporting.** That is the number that
 27→matters for the BO campaign, and it is the first direct measurement of it.
 28→
 29→**On the specific question — do the defects show up? — the honest answer is that
 30→this design cannot tell.** T does fall monotonically from the most-defective to
 31→the least-defective specimen (ρ = −0.90, p = 0.04), but the defect grade is
 32→*identical to the test order*, the felt was adjusted exactly at the defect-group
 33→boundary, and a single specimen's T wanders more within one session (up to
 34→2.34 %) than the five specimens differ from each other (1.95 %). Any of those
 35→three explanations reproduces the observed ranking.
 36→
 37→## 2. Campaign health — all five clean
 38→
 39→| # | specimen | defects | date | captures | cadence | impact at | CH5 raw median %FS | worst TOP axis |
 40→|--:|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
 41→| 1 | `57vqhx` | high | 07-28 | 101 | 40 s | 0.59 ± 0.01 ms | 60.7 % | 27.4 % |
 42→| 2 | `mdt6ja` | high | 07-28 | 100 | 39 s | 0.58 ± 0.01 ms | 68.3 % | 31.0 % |
 43→| 3 | `j1crxg` | high | 07-28 | 100 | 40 s | 0.58 ± 0.00 ms | 70.3 % | 29.7 % |
 44→| 4 | `cruela` | low | 07-29 | 101 | 47 s | 0.70 ± 0.03 ms | 25.0 % | 22.9 % |
 45→| 5 | `bpx68c` | low | 07-29 | 100 | 41 s | 0.65 ± 0.01 ms | 26.4 % | 21.5 % |
 46→
 47→502/502 captures are real drops, no spurious triggers, no channel over full
 48→scale. The 07-28 sessions ran the base sensor at 61–70 % of full scale —
 49→above the FS/3 head-room target and the third-highest loading recorded in the
 50→program, consistent with
 51→[`drop-test-compaction-analysis.md`](drop-test-compaction-analysis.md).
 52→
 53→## 3. Per-specimen results (stabilized drops, burn-in 5)
 54→
 55→| specimen | CH5 input | CV | TOP output | CV | **T = TOP/CH5** | CV |
 56→|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
 57→| `57vqhx` (#1) | 483.3 G | 0.93 % | 504.1 G | 1.00 % | **1.0432** | 0.56 % |
 58→| `mdt6ja` (#2) | 491.0 G | 0.54 % | 509.4 G | 0.89 % | **1.0374** | 0.69 % |
 59→| `j1crxg` (#3) | 493.4 G | 0.32 % | 509.0 G | 0.34 % | **1.0315** | 0.22 % |
 60→| `cruela` (#4) | 456.7 G | 2.28 % | 472.1 G | 2.34 % | **1.0336** | 0.72 % |
 61→| `bpx68c` (#5) | 473.7 G | 1.19 % | 484.7 G | 1.24 % | **1.0231** | 0.17 % |
 62→
 63→ANOVA on T: F = 176.8, p = 2.0e-92 — the specimens are statistically distinct.
 64→All ten pairwise Welch comparisons are significant at the drop level. That
 65→significance is not the interesting part; the *size* is:
 66→
 67→| metric | within-specimen CV | between-specimen CV | ratio | ICC | spread |
 68→|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
 69→| CH5 input | 1.22 % | 3.11 % | 2.6× | 0.87 | 7.65 % |
 70→| TOP output | 1.30 % | 3.37 % | 2.6× | 0.87 | 7.52 % |
 71→| **T = TOP/CH5** | **0.53 %** | **0.72 %** | **1.4×** | 0.65 | **1.95 %** |
 72→
 73→![variance and confound](../data/drop-tests/print-defects/figures/03_variance_and_confound.png)
 74→
 75→The input and output channels spread 7.5–7.7 % across specimens, but T spreads
 76→only 1.95 % — the bulk of the raw-channel spread is the rig (§5), and T removes
 77→it. **Use T, not the raw output peak, for anything cross-specimen.**
 78→
 79→## 4. Does the defect grade explain the differences? Three rival explanations
 80→
 81→T does rank with defect grade: 1.0432 → 1.0374 → 1.0315 → 1.0336 → 1.0231,
 82→Spearman ρ = −0.90 (p = 0.04) — more defects, higher transmissibility, which is
 83→the physically plausible direction. But:
 84→
 85→**(a) Defect grade *is* the test order.** Specimens were graded 1–5 in exactly
 86→the sequence they were tested, so any progressive rig or operator effect
 87→produces ρ = −0.90 identically. The discriminating evidence is that T declines
 88→monotonically **within each day** as well — 07-28: 1.0432 → 1.0374 → 1.0315;
 89→07-29: 1.0336 → 1.0231 — i.e. across a stack reset *and* across the defect-group
 90→boundary. A sequence effect fits the data at least as well as the defect grade.
 91→
 92→**(b) The felt was adjusted at the group boundary.** @me-madsen notes the felt
 93→was moved/adjusted for specimens 4 and 5 — which are also the low-defect
 94→specimens, and also a different day. The input confirms a large change:
 95→
 96→| | specimens 1–3 (high defect) | specimens 4–5 (low defect) | Δ |
 97→|---|--:|--:|--:|
 98→| CH5 CFC-180 input | 489.2 G | 465.2 G | −4.9 % (p = 3.7e-72) |
 99→| CH5 raw \|peak\| | 6,193 G | 2,471 G | **−60.1 %** |
100→
101→So the −5.7 % output-peak difference between the defect groups is essentially
102→the −4.9 % input difference. The T difference (−0.87 %) survives that, but the
103→input change is large enough that a frequency-dependent effect on T cannot be
104→excluded. `cruela`'s +0.077 %/drop input ramp (R² = 0.88) is the freshly
105→adjusted stack re-compacting, visible as the sharp restart at drop 1:
106→
107→![full series](../data/drop-tests/print-defects/figures/01_full_series.png)
108→
109→**(c) Mount re-seating between specimens.** Each specimen requires re-seating
110→the top-vertex accelerometer. The excursion analysis makes this the strongest
111→rival: within a *single* session, with the mount untouched, the 5-drop rolling
112→mean of T moves by
113→
114→| specimen | T range within the session | as % of session mean |
115→|---|---|--:|
116→| `57vqhx` | 1.0322 → 1.0511 | 1.82 % |
117→| `mdt6ja` | 1.0263 → 1.0481 | 2.10 % |
118→| `j1crxg` | 1.0289 → 1.0362 | 0.71 % |
119→| `cruela` | 1.0232 → 1.0474 | **2.34 %** |
120→| `bpx68c` | 1.0206 → 1.0261 | 0.54 % |
121→
122→**The worst within-session excursion (2.34 %) exceeds the entire
123→between-specimen spread (1.95 %).** These are step-like, not smooth — visible as
124→plateau shifts in the bottom panel of the full-series figure, e.g. `57vqhx`
125→around drop 25 — which is the signature of a mount/coupling re-seat rather than
126→of the specimen changing. Prior work put session-to-session coupling shifts at
127→up to 3.7 % ([`drop-test-500drops-nobot-analysis.md`](drop-test-500drops-nobot-analysis.md)).
128→
129→At the honest unit of replication — the specimen, n = 3 vs 2 — the
130→high-vs-low-defect contrast is not significant for either T (p = 0.29) or the
131→output peak (p = 0.12). The drop-level p-values (1.7e-32, 1.9e-95) are
132→pseudo-replication and should not be quoted as evidence about prints.
133→
134→![specimen distributions](../data/drop-tests/print-defects/figures/02_specimen_distributions.png)
135→
136→## 5. What this means for the BO campaign
137→
138→This is the number the sample-size analysis flagged as missing
139→([`drop-test-sample-size-analysis.md`](drop-test-sample-size-analysis.md):
140→"print-to-print reproducibility of the same geometry isn't characterized yet").
141→It now is:
142→
143→- **Print-to-print CV in T ≈ 0.72 %** (five copies of one geometry, ~95 drops
144→  each), spread 1.95 % worst-to-best.
145→- Repeat drops on one article are only **1.4× tighter** than that, so adding
146→  drops past the existing 5-recorded SOP buys almost nothing for a
147→  *between-design* comparison — **replicate prints** are what buy precision.
148→
149→Replicate prints per geometry for 80 % power at α = 0.05, from CV_between = 0.72 %:
150→
151→| difference in T to resolve | replicate prints |
152→|--:|--:|
153→| 1 % | 9 |
154→| 2 % | 3 |
155→| 3 % | 1 |
156→| ≥5 % | 1 |
157→
158→**Against the between-design differences measured so far:**
159→
160→| comparison | T spread | verdict |
161→|---|--:|---|
162→| 60 in campaign — `prc1kn` / `9GMQYQ` / `7xadt6` | 2.3 % | ⚠️ barely above the 1.95 % print-to-print spread — **needs ~3 prints per geometry** |
163→| 13 in input-output — `yqpmx1` … `n0jdwk` | 24 % | ✅ far above; safe with n = 1 print |
164→
165→That is the actionable consequence: the three-structure ranking in
166→[`drop-test-prc1kn-60in-5felts-analysis.md`](drop-test-prc1kn-60in-5felts-analysis.md)
167→spans 2.3 %, and five copies of a *single* geometry span 1.95 % here. Those
168→rankings should be treated as provisional until they are repeated on replicate
169→prints — the statistical significance in that writeup came from ~95 drops on one
170→article each, which measures the article, not the design.
171→
172→## 6. Recommendations
173→
174→1. **Print ≥3 replicates per geometry** before treating a <5 % T difference as a
175→   design result. For ≥10 % differences a single print is fine.
176→2. **Randomize specimen order** within a session block, and re-grade defects
177→   *blind to test order* — this study's ρ = −0.90 is uninterpretable precisely
178→   because grade and order coincide.
179→3. **Do not adjust the absorber stack mid-study.** If it must be adjusted, drop
180→   a reference specimen immediately before and after so the change is measurable.
181→4. **Re-drop a reference specimen at the start and end of every session** to
182→   bound the mount-seating excursion — §4(c) shows it is currently the single
183→   largest uncertainty in cross-specimen T, larger than the print-to-print
184→   scatter it is competing with.
185→5. **A cleaner defect experiment** is available cheaply: re-test 2–3 of these
186→   same five specimens in *reverse* order in one session on one stack state. If
187→   the ranking holds, it is the prints; if it re-orders with sequence, it is the
188→   rig. That is ~15 min of drops per specimen.
189→6. The 07-28 sessions ran CH5 at 61–70 % FS; the PU replacement
190→   ([`drop-test-pu-configs-analysis.md`](drop-test-pu-configs-analysis.md))
191→   removes that exposure entirely and should be in place before the next
192→   long campaign.
193→
194→## 7. Slow-motion video
195→
196→The upload includes 14 slow-motion clips (~548 MB each, ~7.4 GB total) with XML
197→sidecars, which are committed under
198→[`data/drop-tests/print-defects/video/`](../data/drop-tests/print-defects/video/).
199→Every sidecar states `captureFps="959.04p"`, so the time base is exact and needs
200→no pulldown detective work — the same as the `prc1kn` clips
201→([`drop-test-prc1kn-video-analysis.md`](drop-test-prc1kn-video-analysis.md)).
202→
203→Two notes on the set: the file `57cqhx 3.MP4` is a typo for `57vqhx 3`, and
204→`57vqhx 1.XML` has no matching MP4, so specimen 1 has 2 clips rather than 3.
205→Frame-by-frame kinematics were **not run in this pass** — the video bulk is
206→~7.4 GB against a marginal expected return, since the previous two video passes
207→established the rig physics (1–2 ms contact, brake catch, elastic recovery) and
208→confirmed 960 fps cannot resolve peak compression inside the pulse. It is worth
209→doing for a specific question — e.g. whether the defective specimens visibly
210→deform differently — and that is a targeted re-run of the existing
211→`drop_test_prc1kn_video_analysis.py` on 2–3 named clips.
212→
213→## 8. Caveats
214→
215→- **Defect grade is fully confounded with test order, session day and stack
216→  state.** No amount of analysis fixes that; §6.5 is the fix.
217→- **n = 1 physical article per defect grade**, so the defect effect is estimated
218→  from 5 specimens total — the specimen-level contrast (3 vs 2) has almost no
219→  power.
220→- **Defect grading is qualitative** (@me-madsen's visual assessment from the
221→  PR #35 photos/video), not a measured defect metric; a quantitative proxy
222→  (mass, strut straightness, tendon tension) would make the regression meaningful.
223→- **Mount re-seating is not separable from the print** in this design; the
224→  between-specimen CV of 0.72 % is therefore an **upper bound** on true
225→  print-to-print scatter, and the real figure could be considerably smaller.
226→- 20 ms window only, so no ringdown beyond ~18 ms; the pulse onset is truncated
227→  by the trigger, making Δv a captured Δv (6.3–6.5 m/s vs 5.47 m/s free fall
228→  from 60 in, the excess being rebound).
229→- Tri-axis orientation at the top vertex is assumed, not verified.

messages.content:
1→# Can the drop tower measure per-specimen energy absorption? A review and a metrics primer
  2→
  3→**Requested by:** @me-madsen on
  4→[issue #94](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/issues/94),
  5→2026-08-06. **Scope:** the current drop-tower setup and the data recorded so
  6→far — the ABC × 123 crossover captures described on
  7→[PR #86](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/pull/86#issuecomment-5199261361)
  8→(4 channels: CH2–CH4 top-vertex tri-axis output, CH5 base-plate input;
  9→1.25 MHz, 100 ms records, 2 ms pre-trigger) plus the slow-motion video work
 10→— judged against the campaign goal: **optimize T3 prism structures for
 11→energy absorption.**
 12→
 13→All in-repo numbers quoted below come from
 14→[`docs/drop-test-abc123-blind-analysis.md`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/copilot/add-drop-test-protocol-again/docs/drop-test-abc123-blind-analysis.md)
 15→and its committed per-drop metrics.
 16→
 17→---
 18→
 19→## 1. The energy ledger of one drop
 20→
 21→The instrumented plate carrying the specimen falls 60 in and arrests on the
 22→PU mat stack. Kinetic energy at impact is
 23→
 24→```
 25→E_in = ½ M v²,   v = Δv ≈ 5.47 m/s (healthy tower)  →  E_in ≈ 15.0 · M joules
 26→```
 27→
 28→with `M` the total falling mass — **which is not logged anywhere in the
 29→repo**, so no energy in this program is currently expressible in joules.
 30→That energy is partitioned, per drop, into:
 31→
 32→1. **PU mat hysteresis** — the dominant sink by far; it is what turns a
 33→   ~5.5 m/s arrest into a 1.7–3.2 ms, few-hundred-G pulse.
 34→2. **Tower losses** (rail/pin friction, structural damage) — normally
 35→   small, but issue #92 showed a damaged tower silently eating **26–38 %**
 36→   of the drop energy. Larger than everything specimen-related combined.
 37→3. **Fixture/plate dissipation** — unquantified, assumed small.
 38→4. **The specimen** — which receives only a small slice of vibrational
 39→   energy through its base, rings at ~500–550 Hz for 5–13 ms, and hops off
 40→   the plate at ~2–3 % of the impact velocity.
 41→
 42→The specimen never enters large deformation. It responds elastically,
 43→rings, and settles. **The rig is a shock-transmission screen (the geometry
 44→of ASTM D1596 cushion testing, with the specimen riding as the
 45→"product"), not an energy-absorption test.** That is not a criticism — a
 46→transmission screen is exactly the right instrument for the questions it
 47→has been answering (repeatability, discriminability, blind
 48→classification, 18/18) — but it bounds what "energy absorption" can mean
 49→per specimen.
 50→
 51→## 2. Verdict: what is and is not per-specimen measurable
 52→
 53→**Not measurable with the current setup and data, by any reprocessing:**
 54→
 55→- **Energy absorbed by the specimen, in joules.** The specimen's share of
 56→  the ledger is small, entangled with the mat and rig, and the masses
 57→  needed to convert accelerations to energies (carriage, specimen, vertex
 58→  effective mass) were never recorded.
 59→- **Energy absorption in the crashworthiness sense** — the quantity a T3
 60→  prism designed as an absorber is actually for: work done through large
 61→  deformation (strut buckling, snap-through, densification). The current
 62→  test never loads the specimen into that regime, so the campaign
 63→  objective is currently probed only through small-strain, linear-dynamics
 64→  proxies.
 65→
 66→**Measurable per specimen, and now demonstrated repeatable:**
 67→
 68→| quantity | what it is physically | status in our data |
 69→|---|---|---|
 70→| `ζ` (ringdown damping ratio) | fraction of the specimen's *vibrational* energy dissipated per cycle (§3.6) | 5.7–11.4 %, repeats to 0.5–1.7 % absolute where r² ≥ 0.85 |
 71→| `f_n` (ringdown frequency) | dominant modal stiffness-to-mass; for tensegrity, also a **prestress readout** (§3.5) | 500–550 Hz on good fits; cross-arrangement comparison not yet trustworthy |
 72→| `e_rebound` | restitution-like partition of impact into the vertex hop (§3.7) | 0.019–0.030; the one quantity that transferred across sessions and the tower-damage split |
 73→| `T` (peak ratio) | level of shock reaching the top vertex (§3.4) | ~0.99–1.02; repeatable but the *weakest* discriminator in the dataset |
 74→
 75→`ζ` and `e_rebound` are genuine energy-dissipation *proxies* and are
 76→defensible optimization signals for "attenuate/dissipate shock" — but
 77→they measure dissipation of the small vibrational slice, not absorption of
 78→drop energy. If the campaign objective is literally energy absorption,
 79→one of the direct measurements in §4 needs to enter the loop.
 80→
 81→## 3. Metrics primer
 82→
 83→### 3.1 Δv — velocity change (input)
 84→
 85→`Δv = ∫ a_base dt` over the pulse. Equals the arrest velocity of the
 86→plate, so it doubles as a free rig-health gauge (≈ 5.4–5.5 m/s from 60 in
 87→on a healthy tower; the pin-break sessions read 4.2–4.9). Ties to energy
 88→only through the unlogged mass: `E_in = ½MΔv²`. Note (per the J211 audit)
 89→Δv is a processing-dependent descriptor — its value shifts with baseline
 90→and integration window — so it is a monitor, not a calibration.
 91→
 92→### 3.2 Pulse width τ (FWHM) and `f·τ`
 93→
 94→Duration of the base pulse at half its peak. A *shape* metric — invariant
 95→to overall level — which is why it survived an unlogged 22 % energy change
 96→and carried the blind classification. `f_n·τ` locates the specimen on the
 97→shock-response spectrum: our τ = 1.7–3.2 ms against f_n ≈ 520 Hz gives
 98→`f·τ ≈ 0.9–1.7`, near the SRS peak — the specimen neither isolates nor
 99→strongly amplifies; it rides the pulse and rings afterwards. (The old
100→`f·τ ≤ 1.5 ⇒ quasi-static` rule of thumb was checked and refuted in the
101→#86 adversarial review.)
102→
103→### 3.3 SRS — shock response spectrum
104→
105→The standard language for "what does this shock do to hardware?": imagine
106→an array of single-degree-of-freedom oscillators of varying natural
107→frequency riding the measured base pulse; plot each one's peak response
108→against its frequency. Defined in ISO 18431-4 and MIL-STD-810 Method 516;
109→[Tom Irvine's free tutorial](https://www.vibrationdata.com/tutorials2/srs_intr.pdf)
110→is the best entry point. An *input-conditioned output SRS* remains the
111→recommended replacement for `T` as a transmission metric.
112→
113→### 3.4 `T` — CFC-filtered peak ratio (the "transmissibility" misnomer)
114→
115→```
116→T = max|a_out,filtered| / max|a_in,filtered|
117→```
118→
119→with `a_out` the tri-axis vector magnitude at the top vertex and `a_in`
120→the single-axis base channel, both through a CFC low-pass. Three cautions,
121→all now independently established in this repo's audits: (1) the two
122→peaks are **not simultaneous** and the output is a nonlinear magnitude, so
123→this is not transmissibility in any standard (SAE J211, ISO 6487,
124→ISO 18431, ASTM D3332/D7136, MIL-STD-810 checked — Edison audit
125→`6af9d904`); call it a *filtered peak-acceleration ratio*. (2) Its value
126→is filter- and baseline-dependent (the CFC implementation bug and the
127→baseline-window sensitivity both moved it). (3) Empirically it is the
128→weakest specimen discriminator we have. True **transmissibility** is a
129→frequency-response function `|H(f)| = |X_out(f)/X_in(f)|` with a coherence
130→estimate — it needs averaged broadband or repeated excitation (shaker or
131→tap testing), which the single-transient drop does not provide.
132→
133→### 3.5 `f_n` — ringdown natural frequency
134→
135→After the pulse, the specimen vibrates freely at (approximately) its
136→dominant natural frequency, `f_n ≈ (1/2π)√(k_eff/m_eff)`. We estimate it
137→from the slope of the analytic (Hilbert) phase of the band-passed
138→ringdown, which gives sub-bin resolution on short records. Two readings
139→matter for this campaign:
140→
141→- **For a tensegrity structure, `f_n` is a prestress gauge.** Natural
142→  frequencies of tensegrities shift measurably with member self-stress —
143→  the basis of vibration-based tension assessment
144→  ([Ashwear & Eriksson 2014](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260156059_Natural_frequencies_describe_the_pre-stress_in_tensegrity_structures);
145→  demonstrated by modal-hammer tests on a tensegrity *simplex* — the T3
146→  prism topology — in
147→  [Appl. Sci. 10:8733, 2020](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/10/23/8733),
148→  open access). So per-specimen `f_n` drift is a print-tension /
149→  wax-mount health metric, and potentially a design-variable readout.
150→- **Current caveat:** across arrangements our fitted `f_n` ranged
151→  317–552 Hz with specimen orderings that flip — the estimate still
152→  carries input-spectrum and multi-mode contamination. Standardizing on
153→  arrangement B removes the input variation; a bench tap test (specimen
154→  suspended, no tower) would give the clean modal reference the
155→  adversarial review asked for.
156→
157→### 3.6 `ζ` — ringdown decay fit (the closest thing we have to an energy-dissipation measurement)
158→
159→Model the free decay as a damped sinusoid:
160→
161→```
162→x(t) ≈ A e^(−ζ ω_n t) cos(ω_d t + φ),   ω_n = 2π f_n,  ω_d = ω_n √(1−ζ²)
163→```
164→
165→Take the band-passed ringdown, form its Hilbert envelope, fit a line to
166→`ln(envelope)`; the slope is `−ζω_n`, giving the damping ratio `ζ`.
167→Equivalent classical quantities: logarithmic decrement
168→`δ = 2πζ/√(1−ζ²)` (amplitude ratio of successive cycles = `e^−δ`), quality
169→factor `Q = 1/(2ζ)`, and — the energy statement — **fraction of
170→vibrational energy dissipated per cycle**:
171→
172→```
173→ΔE/E per cycle = 1 − e^(−2δ) ≈ 4πζ  (small ζ)
174→```
175→
176→At our fitted ζ ≈ 6–8 % and f_n ≈ 520 Hz that is **~50–60 % of the
177→vibrational energy dissipated every cycle**, envelope time-constant
178→`1/(ζω_n) ≈ 4–5 ms — which is exactly why the usable ringdown is only
179→5–13 ms long. Validity checklist (all enforced in
180→[`drop_test_abc123_blind_analysis.py`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/copilot/add-drop-test-protocol-again/scripts/analysis/drop_test_abc123_blind_analysis.py)):
181→single-mode band selection, fit window ending before the secondary event,
182→r² reported — **a ζ with r² < ~0.85 is not a damping ratio**, it is the
183→estimator reporting that the envelope is not one decaying mode (B1, B2,
184→C1 in the current data). Textbook treatments: Inman, *Engineering
185→Vibration* (log decrement); Ewins, *Modal Testing* (FRF/half-power);
186→Feldman, *Hilbert Transform Applications in Mechanical Vibration* (the
187→envelope method itself).
188→
189→### 3.7 `t_second` and `e_rebound` — the hop
190→
191→Every record shows the top vertex separating and landing back
192→`t_second` = 17–35 ms after impact. Ballistic flight gives the separation
193→velocity `v_sep = g·t_second/2`, and normalizing by impact velocity:
194→
195→```
196→e_rebound = v_sep/Δv = g·t_second/(2Δv)
197→```
198→
199→This is mathematically identical to measuring a coefficient of
200→restitution from time-between-bounces — a classic technique
201→([Bernstein, *Am. J. Phys.* 45:41, 1977](https://pubs.aip.org/aapt/ajp/article-pdf/45/1/41/11809656/41_1_online.pdf),
202→free PDF). Energy view: the hop returns only `e²` (≈ 0.04–0.09 %) of the
203→corresponding kinetic-energy scale — i.e. the vertex-plate interaction is
204→almost totally dissipative — and `e_rebound` measures the *partition*, a
205→dimensionless specimen constant (0.019/0.022–0.024/0.028–0.030 for
206→specimens 2/1/3) that survived the session and tower-damage changes.
207→Open question, already scheduled: the restrained-vs-unrestrained check
208→decides whether it characterizes the structure or the fixture interface.
209→
210→### 3.8 The vocabulary the campaign objective actually lives in
211→
212→For optimizing an absorber, the standard quantities (all defined in
213→Lu & Yu, *Energy Absorption of Structures and Materials*) are:
214→
215→- **Absorbed energy** `E_abs = ∮F dx` — area of the loading–unloading
216→  force-displacement hysteresis loop;
217→- **SEA** = `E_abs`/mass — the usual optimization objective;
218→- **Plateau (mean crush) stress** and **densification strain**;
219→- **Crush-force efficiency** = mean force / peak force — high CFE means
220→  energy absorbed without transmitting a high peak (the absorber ideal);
221→- **Cushion curve** — peak transmitted G vs static loading, per drop
222→  height and thickness (ASTM D1596), and the **damage
223→  boundary/fragility** framing of ASTM D3332.
224→
225→None of these is computable from the current captures. All are computable
226→from §4.
227→
228→## 4. Three upgrade paths to a true energy-absorption measurement
229→
230→**A. Quasi-static compression (recommended first).** Load frame,
231→compress each specimen through its working stroke, record F–d,
232→integrate the hysteresis loop → `E_abs`, SEA, CFE per specimen. This is
233→precisely the protocol of the closest paper to this program —
234→[Pajunen, Johanns, Pal, Rimoli & Daraio, "Design and impact response of
235→3D-printable tensegrity-inspired structures," *Materials & Design* 182
236→(2019) 107966](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127519304046)
237→([open-access version](https://authors.library.caltech.edu/96998)) —
238→which characterized 3D-printed tensegrity-inspired cells by quasi-static
239→compression *plus* drop-weight impact and showed the two agree on the
240→mechanism. Caveat: PU-printed material is rate-dependent, so quasi-static
241→numbers complement rather than replace dynamic ones. Cost: load-frame
242→access; specimens likely survive if kept short of densification.
243→
244→**B. Instrumented direct impact.** Drop a *known mass* fitted with the
245→existing accelerometer directly onto the specimen: `F = M_imp·a`,
246→integrate once for velocity, twice for displacement, and the F–d loop per
247→impact gives **absorbed energy per impact in joules**, plus a
248→carriage-level coefficient of restitution from `v_rebound/v_impact`.
249→This is the energy bookkeeping of drop-weight impact standards
250→(ASTM D7136's instrumented-impactor method). It converts the existing
251→tower with minimal hardware, but it is a real protocol change and loads
252→specimens much harder — sacrifice articles first.
253→
254→**C. Slow-motion velocimetry on the current test.** The slo-mo has so far
255→been used for event timing (brake catch at +76–89 ms). Its higher use is
256→**velocity**: a marker on the carriage, a calibrated length scale in
257→frame, and a known frame rate give incident and rebound velocity, hence
258→stack-level absorbed energy `½M(v_in² − v_out²)` per drop — once `M` is
259→logged. Per-*specimen* differencing this way will almost certainly drown
260→in mat/rig variability (the specimen's share is too small), so treat C as
261→a rig/stack energy audit and a Δv cross-check, not a specimen metric.
262→A photogate or encoder does the same job with less analysis.
263→
264→**Metadata to start logging now, cost ≈ zero:** carriage/falling mass,
265→specimen mass (each print), mat mass and batch, drop height per session
266→(already agreed), first-block Δv (already adopted as the health gauge).
267→
268→## 5. Reading list
269→
270→**Tensegrity impact & energy absorption**
271→- [Pajunen et al., *Mater. Des.* 182:107966 (2019)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127519304046) · [open access](https://authors.library.caltech.edu/96998) — 3D-printed tensegrity-inspired structures under quasi-static compression and drop-weight impact; the closest published analogue of this campaign. Pajunen's [PhD thesis](https://thesis.caltech.edu/13754/9/Thesis_Kirsti_Pajunen_6-2-2020_Full.pdf) (free) extends it to dynamics of tensegrity-inspired metamaterials.
272→- [Rimoli, "On the impact tolerance of tensegrity-based planetary landers," AIAA SciTech 2016-1511](https://arc.aiaa.org/doi/abs/10.2514/6.2016-1511) — virtual drop tests with post-buckling strut behavior; why tensegrity absorbs impact at all.
273→- [SUPERball: Sabelhaus et al., ICRA 2015 / NASA NTRS (free PDF)](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20140011157/downloads/20140011157.pdf) — the flagship tensegrity-lander hardware program.
274→- [Ashwear & Eriksson, *Comput. Struct.* 138:162 (2014)](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260156059_Natural_frequencies_describe_the_pre-stress_in_tensegrity_structures) — natural frequencies as a prestress readout.
275→- [Obara et al., *Appl. Sci.* 10:8733 (2020), open access](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/10/23/8733) — modal-hammer testing of a tensegrity simplex (T3 topology) at different self-stress levels; the experimental template for a bench `f_n` measurement.
276→
277→**Shock, vibration, and damping fundamentals**
278→- [Irvine, "An Introduction to the Shock Response Spectrum" (free PDF)](https://www.vibrationdata.com/tutorials2/srs_intr.pdf) — and the wider [vibrationdata.com](https://www.vibrationdata.com) tutorial library.
279→- Lalanne, *Mechanical Vibration and Shock Analysis*, Vol. 2: *Mechanical Shock* (Wiley) — the reference monograph for pulse shapes, SRS, and drop testing.
280→- Harris & Piersol, *Harris' Shock and Vibration Handbook* (McGraw-Hill) — encyclopedic; chapters on shock data analysis and package cushioning.
281→- Inman, *Engineering Vibration* (Pearson) — log decrement, SDOF damping.
282→- Ewins, *Modal Testing: Theory, Practice and Application* (Wiley) — FRFs, coherence, half-power damping.
283→- Feldman, *Hilbert Transform Applications in Mechanical Vibration* (Wiley, 2011) — the envelope/instantaneous-phase method our ringdown fit uses.
284→- Lu & Yu, [*Energy Absorption of Structures and Materials* (Woodhead, 2003)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/book/9781855736887/energy-absorption-of-structures-and-materials) — SEA, CFE, plateau stress, and design of absorbers.
285→
286→**Standards**
287→- SAE J211-1 — instrumentation for impact tests (CFC filters; see the audited notes in [`edison-trajectories/j211-audit/`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/tree/claude/issue-94-20260806-0326/edison-trajectories/j211-audit)).
288→- ISO 18431-4 — shock-response spectrum analysis. · MIL-STD-810 Method 516 (freely downloadable via EverySpec) — shock testing and SRS practice.
289→- [ASTM D1596](https://www.astm.org/Standards/D1596.htm) — dynamic shock cushioning (our rig's geometry); ASTM D3332 — mechanical-shock fragility (damage boundary); ASTM D7136 — instrumented drop-weight impact (the §4B bookkeeping).
290→- ISO 5348:2021 — accelerometer mounting.
291→
292→**Coefficient of restitution from timing**
293→- [Bernstein, *Am. J. Phys.* 45:41 (1977), free PDF](https://pubs.aip.org/aapt/ajp/article-pdf/45/1/41/11809656/41_1_online.pdf) — COR from time between bounces; the math behind `e_rebound`. Follow-ups: [Aguiar & Laudares, *Am. J. Phys.* 71:499 (2003)](https://www.if.ufrj.br/~carlos/artigos/AJP2003_listening.pdf).
294→
295→---
296→
297→*Prepared for issue #94; no analysis scripts or published numbers were
298→modified. Companion docs: the metric-by-metric audit trail lives in
299→[`docs/drop-test-abc123-blind-analysis.md`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/copilot/add-drop-test-protocol-again/docs/drop-test-abc123-blind-analysis.md)
300→and the standards audit in the j211-audit trajectory.*

1→# SOBOL + S0 BO-campaign drop tests
 2→
 3→First batch of the optimization campaign (announced on PR #86, 08-19-2026):
 4→8 of 9 specimens of the SOBOL + S0 batch, run through the standing SOP —
 5→
 6→- 60 in drop height, arrangement B (1/2 in polyurethane mat,
 7→  [material/specs](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/issues/88#issuecomment-5094675931))
 8→- 101 drops per specimen (first 2 discarded as warm-up at analysis time)
 9→- capture: CH2–CH4 top-vertex tri-axis + CH5 base-plate input, 1.25 MHz,
10→  125,000 samples = 100 ms, 2 ms pre-trigger, 150 G trigger on CH5 —
11→  the settings verified after the 08-18 TP4 reset
12→  (see [`calibration-check/`](../calibration-check/))
13→
14→Analysis writeup:
15→[`docs/drop-test-sobol-campaign-analysis.md`](../../../docs/drop-test-sobol-campaign-analysis.md).
16→Design parameters per specimen: [`params.json`](params.json) (joined from
17→the issue-#98 print key; `amdjwm` is unmapped — see the writeup §5).
18→
19→## Sessions (raw data on Box, ~8.4 GB total)
20→
21→One subfolder per session under [`raw/`](raw/), each holding the TP4
22→**series table** and a **`box-ids.json`** manifest (shared-link name +
23→per-file Box IDs) — the full Signal CSVs stay on Box and can be re-fetched
24→with `scripts/fetch_box_shared_folder.py <shared_name> <dest>`:
25→
26→| session folder | captures | date | Box link |
27→|---|--:|---|---|
28→| `bag26v 8-13-2026 101drops` | 101 | 08-13 | [n5fkbur…](https://byu.box.com/s/n5fkbur86gzronh04rf3f00diw0yz2es) |
29→| `amdjwm-s1 8-17-2026 am 87drops` | 87 | 08-17 | [ig3vgyl…](https://byu.box.com/s/ig3vgyld9t4kbuf2tstvg8v3m2jrwns0) |
30→| `amdjwm 8-17-2026 pm 101drops` | 101 | 08-17 | [xd2ftvi…](https://byu.box.com/s/xd2ftvi3y57jopvxyg1pae7qx61jdsvu) |
31→| `bpx68c 8-17-2026 101drops` | 101 | 08-17 | [it5499h…](https://byu.box.com/s/it5499hkyw24twg7179smsn0fv0bodal) |
32→| `autv5r 8-19-2026 103signals` | 103 | 08-19 | [2uztrfb…](https://byu.box.com/s/2uztrfbblzzwhefmdelt523v4xi1exz0) |
33→| `6lhxfy-s1 8-19-2026 35drops` | 35 | 08-19 | [hkyw0nv…](https://byu.box.com/s/hkyw0nv9s2l27r893sapb6kxumk0l0d9) |
34→| `6lhxfy 8-20-2026 101drops` | 101 | 08-20 | [q5tyg1a…](https://byu.box.com/s/q5tyg1as1h0pgqrppa8nsuhnllbhjsnu) |
35→| `9hhbkp 8-20-2026 101drops` | 101 | 08-20 | [bbwutg2…](https://byu.box.com/s/bbwutg2r6a4l3q71vv2q84nvrue7h1h6) |
36→| `nvxsrv 8-20-2026 101drops` | 101 | 08-20 | [cym881r…](https://byu.box.com/s/cym881rlx1je5rec4eowj8khglopax2i) |
37→| `6nheas 8-20-2026 101drops` | 101 | 08-20 | [y7v10k0…](https://byu.box.com/s/y7v10k08mqb3f093dxfl4pn8wafq6n9i) |
38→
39→`-s1` suffix = interrupted first session (kept as an independent
40→session-repeatability check; excluded from the campaign summary). `bpx68c`
41→08-17 is the same upload as the calibration-check "before" set.
42→
43→## Outputs (committed under `figures/`)
44→
45→- `campaign_summary.csv` — one row per specimen, objectives ± sd + design
46→  parameters: **the BO ingest file**
47→- `campaign_metrics.json` — full record incl. per-drop rows
48→  (`partial_sessions_metrics.json` for the two `-s1` sessions)
49→- `01_campaign_series.png`, `02_campaign_ranking.png`
50→
51→## Reproducing
52→
53→```bash
54→pip install numpy scipy matplotlib
55→# fetch each session listed above into a subfolder of raw/, then:
56→python scripts/analysis/drop_test_campaign_analysis.py --procs 4 \
57→    --params "data/drop-tests/sobol-campaign/params.json"
58→```
59→
60→Note the pipeline uses the **tail baseline** (`analyze_capture(...,
61→baseline="tail")`): from 08-17 on, mat contact starts > 2 ms before the
62→150 G trigger, so the pre-trigger window rides a +10–20 G contact foot and
63→is not a valid zero. Validated against the TP4 series tables (writeup §2).

1→"""Multi-objective BO for the T-3_01 prism campaign: ingest drop results, suggest next batch.
  2→
  3→Generated from the Honegumi template (https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.06815,
  4→https://honegumi.readthedocs.io) with options: objective=Multi,
  5→model=Fully Bayesian (SAASBO), existing_data=True, synchrony=Batch,
  6→visualize=True, custom_gen=True (required by the fully Bayesian choice);
  7→all constraint/categorical/fidelity/task options False. The template pins
  8→ax-platform==0.4.3; this script runs unchanged on ax-platform 0.5.0 (same
  9→Service API). Deviations from the rendered template, each forced by the
 10→real campaign rather than preference:
 11→
 12→1. The Sobol initialization step is dropped from the GenerationStrategy
 13→   because it already happened physically: PR #35's ``t3_prism_sobol_batch.py``
 14→   drew the 9-point Sobol batch (seed 0) that was printed and tested. The
 15→   strategy therefore starts directly at the SAASBO step.
 16→2. The inline ``X_train``/``y_train`` dataframe is replaced by ingestion of
 17→   the measured campaign summary (``t3-prism-bo-batch-drop-results.csv``,
 18→   snapshotted from PR #86 branch commit 642b8c0, file
 19→   ``data/drop-tests/sobol-campaign/figures/campaign_summary.csv``).
 20→3. The optimization loop body does not evaluate a dummy objective: the
 21→   "experiment" is a physical print + 101-drop session, so the loop runs
 22→   exactly once, records the suggested batch to CSV, and exits. Results get
 23→   reported back by re-running this script once the next batch is tested.
 24→
 25→Search space: the base Sobol coordinates from PR #35's generator (not the
 26→as-printed geometry). Each suggestion is a 5-vector (R, H, twist, strut d,
 27→cable d) that feeds straight into ``t3_prism_sobol_batch.py``'s constant-mass
 28→projection to produce printable STLs, exactly like round 1.
 29→
 30→Objectives (both minimized), per the campaign analysis doc's BO hand-off
 31→section (docs/drop-test-sobol-campaign-analysis.md on PR #86) and the
 32→energy-absorption review (PR #97):
 33→
 34→* ``t180``: stabilized CFC-180 transmissibility TOP/CH5 (shock into payload).
 35→* ``e_rebound``: rebound energy ratio (energy returned to the payload as a
 36→  hop instead of absorbed). The 8-specimen data shows these trade off (the
 37→  best attenuator hops hardest), so the Pareto front is informative.
 38→
 39→Ingestion notes, current as of the 2026-08-21 upload (8 of 9 specimens):
 40→
 41→* ``amdjwm`` maps to no known print ID or Sobol spec (open item 1 in the
 42→  campaign doc), so it cannot be attached and is skipped with a warning.
 43→  Re-run once identified; its row already carries the objectives.
 44→* The S0 reference prism ``bpx68c`` is off-Sobol but its base coordinates
 45→  (25, 70, 60, 6, 3) sit inside the search space, so it is attached.
 46→* Printed-but-untested specs (03, 06, 07) are attached as pending trials so
 47→  the acquisition avoids re-suggesting near them.
 48→
 49→Usage (from the repo root)::
 50→
 51→    pip install ax-platform==0.5.0 pandas matplotlib
 52→    python bo/t3_prism_bo_campaign.py            # writes suggestions + figure
 53→    python bo/t3_prism_bo_campaign.py --batch-size 9 --round 1
 54→"""
 55→
 56→from __future__ import annotations
 57→
 58→import argparse
 59→import sys
 60→from pathlib import Path
 61→
 62→import numpy as np
 63→import pandas as pd
 64→from ax.core.observation import ObservationFeatures
 65→from ax.modelbridge.factory import Models
 66→from ax.modelbridge.generation_strategy import GenerationStep, GenerationStrategy
 67→from ax.service.ax_client import AxClient, ObjectiveProperties
 68→import matplotlib
 69→
 70→matplotlib.use("Agg")
 71→import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
 72→
 73→BO_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
 74→
 75→# define these names as variables for reuse (Honegumi convention)
 76→obj1_name = "t180"
 77→obj2_name = "e_rebound"
 78→
 79→PARAM_NAMES = ["R_mm", "H_mm", "twist_deg", "strut_d_mm", "cable_d_mm"]
 80→
 81→# Search space: identical to PARAMETERS in bo/t3_prism_sobol_batch.py (PR #35),
 82→# the space the printed Sobol batch was drawn from.
 83→PARAMETERS = [
 84→    {"name": "R_mm", "type": "range", "bounds": [25.0, 40.0], "value_type": "float"},
 85→    {"name": "H_mm", "type": "range", "bounds": [60.0, 110.0], "value_type": "float"},
 86→    {"name": "twist_deg", "type": "range", "bounds": [40.0, 80.0], "value_type": "float"},
 87→    {"name": "strut_d_mm", "type": "range", "bounds": [6.0, 12.0], "value_type": "float"},
 88→    {"name": "cable_d_mm", "type": "range", "bounds": [3.0, 5.5], "value_type": "float"},
 89→]
 90→
 91→# Base coordinates of the S0 reference prism (bpx68c): the T3 base design,
 92→# printed at uniform scale 1.1538 (issue #98, 2026-08-17). In-bounds, so it
 93→# is valid existing data even though it was not part of the Sobol draw.
 94→S0_BASE_PARAMS = {
 95→    "R_mm": 25.0,
 96→    "H_mm": 70.0,
 97→    "twist_deg": 60.0,
 98→    "strut_d_mm": 6.0,
 99→    "cable_d_mm": 3.0,
100→}
101→
102→
103→def load_training_data(results_path: Path, design_path: Path):
104→    """Join measured objectives onto base Sobol coordinates.
105→
106→    Returns (X_train, y_train, labels, pending) where pending holds the
107→    base coordinates of designed-and-printed specs with no results yet.
108→    """
109→    results = pd.read_csv(results_path, dtype={"spec": "string"})
110→    design = pd.read_csv(design_path).set_index("specimen")
111→
112→    X_train, y_train, labels = [], [], []
113→    for _, row in results.iterrows():
114→        spec = row["spec"]
115→        spec = None if pd.isna(spec) else str(spec).strip()
116→        if not spec:
117→            print(
118→                f"WARNING: skipping specimen {row['specimen']!r}: no Sobol spec "
119→                "mapping (see campaign doc open item 1). Re-run once identified."
120→            )
121→            continue
122→        if spec == "S0":
123→            params = dict(S0_BASE_PARAMS)
124→        else:
125→            base = design.loc[int(spec)]
126→            params = {name: float(base[name]) for name in PARAM_NAMES}
127→        n = float(row["n_valid"])
128→        # noise passed as SEM of the per-drop series; note the ~2 percent
129→        # print-to-print floor (n = 1 article per design) is NOT captured here
130→        y_train.append(
131→            {
132→                obj1_name: (float(row["t180_mean"]), float(row["t180_sd"]) / np.sqrt(n)),
133→                obj2_name: (
134→                    float(row["e_rebound_mean"]),
135→                    float(row["e_rebound_sd"]) / np.sqrt(n),
136→                ),
137→            }
138→        )
139→        X_train.append(params)
140→        labels.append(f"{row['specimen']} (spec {spec})")
141→
142→    tested_specs = {
143→        int(s) for s in results["spec"].dropna() if str(s).strip() not in ("", "S0")
144→    }
145→    pending = []
146→    for spec_idx in sorted(set(design.index) - tested_specs):
147→        base = design.loc[spec_idx]
148→        pending.append(
149→            (f"spec {spec_idx:02d}", {name: float(base[name]) for name in PARAM_NAMES})
150→        )
151→    return X_train, y_train, labels, pending
152→
153→
154→def main(argv=None):
155→    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
156→    ap.add_argument(
157→        "--results",
158→        type=Path,
159→        default=BO_DIR / "t3-prism-bo-batch-drop-results.csv",
160→        help="campaign summary CSV (snapshot of PR #86 campaign_summary.csv)",
161→    )
162→    ap.add_argument(
163→        "--design",
164→        type=Path,
165→        default=BO_DIR / "t3-prism-bo-batch.csv",
166→        help="Sobol batch design table (base coordinates), from PR #35",
167→    )
168→    ap.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=9, help="prints per round (9 plates)")
169→    ap.add_argument("--round", type=int, default=1, help="suggestion round number, for file names")
170→    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
171→    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
172→
173→    X_train, y_train, labels, pending = load_training_data(args.results, args.design)
174→    n_train = len(X_train)
175→    print(f"Attaching {n_train} completed trials; {len(pending)} printed-but-untested pending.")
176→
177→    # Fully Bayesian (SAASBO) generation strategy. The Sobol step from the
178→    # Honegumi template is omitted: initialization was the physical batch.
179→    gs = GenerationStrategy(
180→        steps=[
181→            GenerationStep(
182→                # https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00349
183→                model=Models.SAASBO,
184→                num_trials=-1,  # no limit on trials (final model step)
185→                max_parallelism=max(args.batch_size, len(pending) + args.batch_size),
186→            ),
187→        ]
188→    )
189→
190→    ax_client = AxClient(generation_strategy=gs, random_seed=args.seed, verbose_logging=False)
191→    ax_client.create_experiment(
192→        name="t3_prism_drop_campaign",
193→        parameters=PARAMETERS,
194→        objectives={
195→            obj1_name: ObjectiveProperties(minimize=True),
196→            obj2_name: ObjectiveProperties(minimize=True),
197→        },
198→    )
199→
200→    # Add existing data to the AxClient
201→    for parameterization, results_i in zip(X_train, y_train):
202→        # signal to Ax that you intend to carry out a particular trial
203→        _, trial_index = ax_client.attach_trial(parameterization)
204→        # pass the (historically available) outcome for that trial
205→        ax_client.complete_trial(trial_index=trial_index, raw_data=results_i)
206→
207→    # printed but not yet tested: attach without completing so the acquisition
208→    # treats them as pending points
209→    pending_indices = {}
210→    for label, parameterization in pending:
211→        _, trial_index = ax_client.attach_trial(parameterization)
212→        pending_indices[trial_index] = label
213→        print(f"  pending trial {trial_index}: {label}")
214→
215→    # one physical round per script run: fit + suggest the next batch
216→    # (note the plural "trials" for batch optimization)
217→    parameterizations, optimization_complete = ax_client.get_next_trials(args.batch_size)
218→
219→    # model predictions (posterior mean +/- sd) for the suggested designs
220→    model = ax_client.generation_strategy.model
221→    obs_feats = [
222→        ObservationFeatures(parameters=dict(p)) for p in parameterizations.values()
223→    ]
224→    f_mean, f_cov = model.predict(obs_feats)
225→
226→    rows = []
227→    for j, (trial_index, parameterization) in enumerate(parameterizations.items()):
228→        row = {"round": args.round, "trial_index": trial_index}
229→        row.update({name: parameterization[name] for name in PARAM_NAMES})
230→        for metric in (obj1_name, obj2_name):
231→            row[f"pred_{metric}_mean"] = f_mean[metric][j]
232→            row[f"pred_{metric}_sd"] = float(np.sqrt(f_cov[metric][metric][j]))
233→        rows.append(row)
234→    suggestions = pd.DataFrame(rows)
235→
236→    out_csv = BO_DIR / f"t3-prism-bo-suggestions-round{args.round}.csv"
237→    suggestions.to_csv(out_csv, index=False, float_format="%.4f")
238→    print(f"\nSuggested batch (recorded to {out_csv}):")
239→    print(suggestions.to_string(index=False))
240→
241→    # persist full experiment state (trials, data, generation strategy)
242→    snapshot = BO_DIR / f"t3-prism-bo-ax-client-round{args.round}.json"
243→    ax_client.save_to_json_file(str(snapshot))
244→    print(f"AxClient snapshot saved to {snapshot}")
245→
246→    # ---- visualization (Honegumi visualize=True block, adapted) ----------
247→    objectives = ax_client.objective_names
248→    df = ax_client.get_trials_data_frame()
249→    observed = df.dropna(subset=objectives)
250→
251→    # use model predictions for Pareto front (better for noisy observations)
252→    pareto = ax_client.get_pareto_optimal_parameters(use_model_predictions=True)
253→    pareto_data = [p[1][0] for p in pareto.values()]
254→    pareto_df = pd.DataFrame(pareto_data).sort_values(objectives[0])
255→
256→    fig, (ax_obj, ax_par) = plt.subplots(
257→        1, 2, figsize=(11.5, 4.6), dpi=200, gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.15, 1]}
258→    )
259→
260→    ax_obj.scatter(
261→        observed[objectives[0]], observed[objectives[1]],
262→        fc="none", ec="#0b0b0b", s=45, label="Observed (round 1)",
263→    )
264→    for label, (_, orow) in zip(labels, observed.iterrows()):
265→        ax_obj.annotate(
266→            label.split(" ")[0], (orow[objectives[0]], orow[objectives[1]]),
267→            textcoords="offset points", xytext=(5, 4), fontsize=7, color="#52514e",
268→        )
269→    ax_obj.plot(
270→        pareto_df[objectives[0]], pareto_df[objectives[1]],
271→        color="#2a78d6", lw=2, marker="o", ms=4, label="Model Pareto front",
272→    )
273→    ax_obj.scatter(
274→        suggestions[f"pred_{obj1_name}_mean"], suggestions[f"pred_{obj2_name}_mean"],
275→        marker="D", s=40, fc="#eb6834", ec="white", lw=0.8,
276→        label=f"Suggested round {args.round + 1} (predicted)", zorder=3,
277→    )
278→    ax_obj.set_xlabel("t180 (CFC-180 transmissibility, lower is better)")
279→    ax_obj.set_ylabel("e_rebound (rebound energy ratio, lower is better)")
280→    ax_obj.set_title("Objective space")
281→    ax_obj.legend(fontsize=8, loc="best")
282→    ax_obj.grid(alpha=0.25, lw=0.5)
283→
284→    # parameter-space panel: min-max normalized parallel coordinates
285→    bounds = {p["name"]: p["bounds"] for p in PARAMETERS}
286→
287→    def normalize(params):
288→        return [
289→            (params[name] - bounds[name][0]) / (bounds[name][1] - bounds[name][0])
290→            for name in PARAM_NAMES
291→        ]
292→
293→    xs = range(len(PARAM_NAMES))
294→    for params in X_train:
295→        ax_par.plot(xs, normalize(params), color="#0b0b0b", alpha=0.35, lw=1.2)
296→    for _, params in pending:
297→        ax_par.plot(xs, normalize(params), color="#52514e", alpha=0.6, lw=1.2, ls=":")
298→    for _, srow in suggestions.iterrows():
299→        ax_par.plot(
300→            xs, normalize({name: srow[name] for name in PARAM_NAMES}),
301→            color="#eb6834", alpha=0.85, lw=1.6,
302→        )
303→    ax_par.plot([], [], color="#0b0b0b", alpha=0.5, lw=1.2, label="Tested")
304→    ax_par.plot([], [], color="#52514e", lw=1.2, ls=":", label="Pending prints")
